fast-uri.rationale: roll-forward 3.1.4 -> 3.1.5 (in-3.x patch) clears GHSA-7p8r-x3mc-p8w7 (host confusion via a malformed authority introducer: '\', '/\' or '\/' used in place of '//' after the scheme colon, which Node's URL parses as a different host; OSV affected [0,2.4.4), [3.0.0,3.1.5), [4.0.0,4.1.2)). Security-only release: the entire runtime diff is index.js +37/-1 adding a MALFORMED_AUTHORITY_INTRODUCER check in parseWithStatus() and making resolve() throw on a malformed authority or port, plus +136 lines of tests. fast-uri is transitive via ajv (JSON-schema $id/$ref URI parsing), NOT used here for host-based policy or SSRF filtering, so the confusion is not exploitable in this closure; the bump clears the advisory regardless. Publisher (matteo.collina), the eleven fastify maintainers, repository and BSD-3-Clause license all unchanged. Stayed on the 3.x line: 4.1.2 is the 4.x fix and a separate major review. See ledger/2026-08-10/fast-uri@3.1.5.md.

hono.rationale: roll-forward 4.12.31 -> 4.12.34 (in-minor patch) clears four advisories, all with fix line 4.12.34: GHSA-54fx-42gc-7vw4 (algorithmic-complexity DoS in the Language middleware), GHSA-79qm-7rj5-m7r9 (Proxy helper does not strip response headers named in Connection), GHSA-8j4g-w8fx-2239 (ReDoS in the CORS middleware via Access-Control-Request-Headers) and GHSA-f23p-vx2j-j53r (memo() retains SSR output across requests). None of the four affected surfaces is loaded here. src/ imports no hono module directly; the only hono consumption is transitive, via the MCP SDK's server/streamableHttp.js importing getRequestListener from @hono/node-server, which itself statically imports exactly one hono submodule, hono/ws (unchanged across this range, and its upgradeWebSocket is never invoked). @hono/node-server never constructs a Hono app or a HonoRequest, so hono's request-parsing layer is not entered either: NO change in 4.12.31..4.12.34 is on a path this gateway executes. Same sole maintainer (yusukebe); SLSA provenance verified to honojs/hono at tag v4.12.34, commit 734755ace341607628219ea1dd8ca17f01bf1a5c. The override was converted from the ^4.12.27 caret to an EXACT 4.12.34, because at the new fix line a caret resolves to the 4.13.x head, which is a minor bump the advisories do not require; release-security-audit.sh's hono floor moved [4,12,27] -> [4,12,34] in lock-step and reads the lockfile, not the override string. See ledger/2026-08-10/hono@4.12.34.md, which records two claims corrected in review.

ip-address.rationale: FIRST INDIVIDUAL REVIEW (the 10.2.0 entry was a 2026-07-10 bootstrap marked 'not individually reviewed'). Roll-forward 10.2.0 -> 10.3.1 clears three advisories: GHSA-22jq-vg5j-6vgg (misclassification of IPv4-mapped/NAT64 IPv6 addresses, fixed 10.2.1), GHSA-4xrf-jv44-h6hh (a CIDR suffix suppresses special-use classification, fixed 10.2.2) and GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr (Address4 decodes leading-zero octets as decimal while resolvers use octal, fixed 10.3.1); 10.3.1 is the highest of the three fix lines. None is reachable here: ip-address arrives only via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk -> express-rate-limit, whose entire use is Address6 for ipKeyGenerator subnet grouping (networkForm()), calling none of the misclassifying predicates, and src/ never imports the SDK auth handlers that load express-rate-limit at all. The range is NOT confined to classification: besides the isHostInSubnet migration of every special-use predicate and the new embeddedIPv4 delegation, it changes Address4.parse to THROW on leading-zero octets, rejects a stacked subnet suffix, fixes the fromURL port-squelch bound, pads toByteArray to 16 bytes, propagates the v4-in-v6 subnet suffix, preserves the to4() prefix, canonicalises groupForV6 and to4in6, and tightens addressMinusSuffix. No new network, filesystem or process capability surface. NOTE the publisher changed from the user token beaugunderson to GitHub Actions trusted publishing with SLSA provenance (attestation verified to beaugunderson/ip-address at tag v10.3.1, commit be7e626c0d49fccb518899f520a3fb64ee189741), and that change is load-bearing: the published 10.2.0 artifact does NOT match its own tag. Three of five sources disagree, including v6/constants.ts, where hardened URL regexes existed at tag v10.2.0 but never reached the artifact. 10.3.1 is the first ip-address artifact in this closure whose contents match the source it claims to be built from. Applied as a NEW exact override since nothing in the tree demanded above 10.2.0 on its own. See ledger/2026-08-10/ip-address@10.3.1.md and REVIEW-LOG.md.
